rv.q: Actors are seldom given space to convey their characters' inner lives; when they are, they shine.

The atmosphere was brought to life having been performed in an open-air theatre. It immersed its audience in the environment and allowed the actors to engage with the audience in a humorous and witty way. Overall, the projection of the cast was very good however some words were lost occasionally due to the wind.
The RSC's apparent reverse-Globe scheduling policy of rarer Shakespeare plays in the summer and the most famous ones in winter continues with Twelfth Night as the holiday show.

cn.t: Critics find this RSC production of "Twelfth Night" musically uplifting but conceptually heavy-handed, with Puwanarajah's direction constraining Shakespeare's nimble romance despite some memorable moments.
